key_decisions.decision: Identifies the space behind the curtain as the inner sanctuary and retains atonement cover from Exodus. The restriction is not an absolute ban on entry, and the death warning and divine cloud remain.
Preserves the parallel lots and untranslated Azazel, leaving its debated referent to a note rather than making scapegoat or a demon name certain.
Retains alive, both occurrences of Azazel, divine presence and the ambiguous atonement-over-it formulation rather than deciding between for it and by means of it.
Retains the testimony rather than replacing it with ark, explains it selectively in vocabulary, and keeps the incense cloud's stated protective purpose.
Distinguishes blood on the east-facing side from seven sprinklings in front. The alternative eastward directional reading is noted, and no first-action count is invented.
Retains sanctuary purification and the distinct impurity/rebellion/sin terms; preserves the tent dwelling among an impure people rather than only among the already clean.
Retains movement outward, both blood sources and all altar horns; does not identify the unnamed altar or supply a mixing procedure.
Preserves both hands, following the read plural alongside written hand, all three wrongdoing terms, transfer to the head and an appointed male escort; ready is an alternative for itti.
Keeps the concrete carrying image and wrongdoing term linked to verse 21; renders cut-off land as remote without adding a cliff or a killing.
Preserves exact date, self-affliction as enacted self-denial, all-work prohibition and equal native/sojourner scope; does not reduce the command to an inward attitude or specify only fasting.
Leaves the unstated atonement agent open and follows the Hebrew accent division attaching from all your sins to the final clean clause; the alternative attachment is noted.
Preserves intensified sabbath rest, repeated self-denial and repeated lasting status without reducing the instruction to a weekly date.
Keeps the inner sanctuary distinct and all five objects or beneficiaries of atonement, preserving the repeated verb without replacing cleansing of places with forgiveness.
Retains once a year, all sins and the narrative past-tense completion; identifies the implicit he as Aaron and records alternatives without inventing a date of performance.
